text:
Drew Doughty is 36, in his 19th season with the only team he has played for, and still logging 21:32 a night. The legacy is secure (two Stanley Cups, a Norris Trophy in 2016), and the question now is how much of the old engine is left.

The recent stretch is quiet. He is pointless in seven straight games, and our numbers say the chances have thinned out too, so we would not call it bad luck. He has seven points in 18 games. At 5v5 the Kings get 46.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, worse than without him.

The defensive case is stronger. Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away at an 88th-percentile rate last season, with most of his value from even-strength defense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 14% of entries at his line against a typical 11%. He missed practice last week before returning. The Athletic's Sean McIndoe included him in a piece on veteran stars who may have played their last playoff game. The minutes say Los Angeles still needs him.
